channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Posts fresh two-month low below 1.3900
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) outperforms a majority of its currency peers on Friday, with the USD/CAD pair trading 0.32% lower at around 1.3888. The Canadian currency gains on hopes of a United States (US)-Canada interim deal.

item.title: WTI Oil rebounds as supply tensions overshadow demand concerns
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil rebounds on Friday and trades around $80.80 at the time of writing, up 0.40% on the day. Oil prices recover some of their losses after two days of correction as investors remain concerned about energy supply disruptions in the Middle East.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Approaches 0.5900 resistance area as US Dollar weakens
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) appreciates on Wednesday as the US Dollar (USD) loses ground across the board amid dwindling hopes of immediate Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.

item.title: UoM Consumer Sentiment Index set to ease as inflation, labour market worries loom
item.description: The University of Michigan (UoM) will release the preliminary estimate of August’s Consumer Sentiment Index on Friday.

item.title: Euro holds gains above 1.1550 following Eurozone GDP and bright Trade Balance data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) holds moderate gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, as Eurozone Gross Domestic Product (GDP) came in line with market forecasts while June's Trade Balance beat forecasts.

item.title: US Dollar: Looking for a shift in Fedspeak – ING
item.description: ING strategists Francesco Pesole, Frantisek Taborsky and Chris Turner note that post-CPI summer conditions are suppressing FX volatility and keeping the Dollar broadly stable. They still see scope for a weaker Dollar as market expectations for further Federal Reserve tightening look overstated.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Bearish bias within 158.00–160.20 band against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann judge USD/JPY price action as inconclusive intraday, with trading expected between 159.00 and 159.70 after a tight 159.01–159.56 range.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $64.76 per troy ounce, up 0.48% from the $64.45 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: Silver regains ground above $64 as Fed rate hike bets fade
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) gains 0.37% on Friday and trades around $64.70 at the time of writing, erasing part of its recent correction.

item.title: Brazilian Real: Election risks threaten Real – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Dev Ashish flags growing election and fiscal risks weighing on Brazilian assets. BRL has underperformed in LatAm, with USD/BRL nearing its 200-day moving average at 5.2042 and Bovespa breaking below its long-term average.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA keeps hike option open – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategist Elwin de Groot reports that the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) left rates unchanged, with markets initially reading the statement as dovish.

item.title: Federal Reserve: RMP pause and QT timing – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Gennadiy Goldberg and Molly Brooks analyze the Federal Reserve’s decision to halt Reserve Management Purchases (RMP) after tapering from $40bn to $10bn per month.

item.title: Eurozone Q2 GDP growth remains at 0.4%, as flash data showed
item.description: According to Eurostat, the Eurozone Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth in the second quarter this year remains at 0.4%, as shown by the preliminary data released on July 30.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: DXY declines to 99.75-99.70 amid receding Fed hike bets
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, continues to lose ground through the first half of the European session on Friday and retreats further from a two-week high, touched the previous day.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Picks up above 1.3500 amid generalised US Dollar weakness
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) pares losses against a weaker US Dollar (USD) on Friday, as a run of soft US inflation figures and growing signs of labour market deterioration have cast doubt about the odds for an immediate Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike.

item.title: British Pound: Growth resilience supports gains against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman reports the British Pound (GBP) is the best performing major currency in August, with GBP/USD back above 1.3500. The United Kingdom (UK) economy is proving resilient to the energy price shock linked to the US-Iran conflict, with Q2 GDP up 0.4% after 0.6% in Q1.

item.title: Indian Rupee flattens while approaching weekend
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades flat at around 95.40 against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday. The USD/INR pair consolidates as investors seek fresh cues regarding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital passage to almost one-fifth of global energy supply, which is keeping oil prices higher.

item.title: US Dollar: Carry trades supported as Fed seen on hold – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that softer United States (US) Producer Price Index (PPI) and lower US Treasury yields have led markets to scale back expectations of a September Federal Reserve (Fed) hike, limiting US Dollar (USD) upside.

item.title: Euro flattens against Japanese Yen, ECB-BoJ to raise rates in September
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades flat at around 183.85 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) during the European trading session on Friday. The cross consolidates while investors seek fresh cues regarding whether there will be more United States (US)-Japan joint intervention to prop up the Japanese currency.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Shifting rate expectations and currency support – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur notes that Japanese government support for an imminent Bank of Japan rate hike has reinforced market expectations rather than surprised them. Probabilities now favor a hike as early as September, with October fully priced and another move in December possible.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI support offsets wider trade gap – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale notes India’s headline CPI rose slightly to 4.45% year-on-year in July, backing the RBI’s decision to keep policy unchanged. The central bank has reportedly been active in FX markets as the trade deficit widened.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Upside risk intact above support against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note AUD/USD is consolidating intraday between 0.7050 and 0.7075 after a brief spike to 0.7091 failed to build momentum.

item.title: Gold recovers intraday losses as reduced Fed hike bets offset geopolitics and weigh on USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) finds decent support ahead of the $4,300 mark and recovers a major part of its intraday losses during the first half of the European session on Friday.

item.title: Brent: Geopolitical premium eases after six-day rally – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank analysts highlight that Brent Oil has finally broken a six-day winning streak, with prices pulling back modestly as some geopolitical risk premium is removed.

item.title: Japanese Yen recovers from two-week low on fast BoJ rate hike bets, softer USD
item.description: The USD/JPY pair sticks to modest intraday losses through the first half of the European session on Friday, though it manages to hold above the 159.00 mark and remains close to a two-week top set the previous day.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Hawkish ECB prospects support Euro
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades 0.17% higher at around 1.1550 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Friday. The major currency pair gains as the Euro rises due to firm expectations that the European Central Bank (ECB) will raise interest rates in the policy meeting in September.

item.title: US Dollar: Softer tone with falling yields – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes the US Dollar (USD) is trading on a softer footing as Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike expectations are scaled back following weaker labour data and a mixed United States (US) Producer Price Index (PPI) report.

item.title: Australian Dollar bounces up, US Dollar droops ahead of US Retail Sales data
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is trading a tad firmer against the Dollar (USD) on Friday, fuelled by hawkish remarks by Reserve Bank of Australia’s (RBA) Assistant Governor, Chris Kent.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ tightening debate supports JPY – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategist Elwin de Groot highlights that Japanese policymakers are increasingly focused on achieving the inflation target sustainably and supporting the Japanese Yen. Following recent FX intervention, He argues that exchange-rate management ultimately needs monetary policy backing.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Weaker after Norges Bank holds rates – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research Team notes that Norges Bank left its policy rate at 4.25% and kept a tightening bias despite weaker summer inflation. They still expect one final hike in September, though the odds have fallen and the decision is now finely balanced.
